news.headline: Bengals' Tee Higgins: No practice Wednesday
news.summary: Higgins sat out Wednesday's practice with a foot/heel issue that Zac Taylor called minor, but it's worth tracking before you lock your Week 3 lineup.

news.headline: Colts WR Alec Pierce will be placed on injured reserve
news.summary: With Pierce headed to IR, Downs steps into the clear No. 1 receiver role for Indianapolis, a real target-share boost for Week 3.

news.headline: Baltimore Ravens Thursday Injury Report: Zay Flowers Returns to Practice
news.summary: Flowers was limited by hamstring tightness again Wednesday but returned to practice Thursday, and the Ravens reportedly like his chances to play Sunday in Rio.

news.headline: NFL field director confident Rio stadium surface in good shape
news.summary: Six weeks of heavy rain left the Maracaã pitch rough, but the NFL's field director says he's confident it'll be ready, easing (not eliminating) the field-condition risk for Sunday's kicking game.

news.headline: George Pickens looking to 'get the mission done' vs. Ravens in Rio
news.summary: Pickens is healthy and locked in for Sunday's Rio matchup, which carries the week's second-highest total despite ongoing field-condition concerns at the Maracanã.

news.headline: Giants QB Jaxson Dart to undergo season-ending knee surgery
news.summary: Dart's knee damage is confirmed season-ending, cementing Jameis Winston as the Giants' full-time starter and reshaping the receiving-usage outlook for Likely the rest of the way.

news.headline: Fantasy football Week 3 RB preview: Travis Etienne appears to have an Alvin Kamara problem
news.summary: Etienne was limited Wednesday with a hamstring issue, and Kamara is now clearly out-touching him in the Saints backfield — a real floor concern heading into Week 3.

news.headline: Parker Washington - Fantasy Football Risers, Breakouts for Week 3
news.summary: Washington reportedly missed most of this week's practice with an undisclosed injury, but is expected back and remains Jacksonville's top passing-game option vs. New England — worth a Friday recheck.

news.headline: 49ers vs. Cardinals report: Brock Purdy questionable for Week 3
news.summary: Purdy returned to practice only as a limited participant and Kyle Shanahan called it 'highly unlikely' he starts Sunday, while Nick Bosa's Wednesday absence was a scheduled rest day, not a new injury — no threat to the defense's floor.

news.headline: Saints' Devaughn Vele: Still tending to hip injury
news.summary: Vele was limited Wednesday with a hip injury he's still managing — worth monitoring if he's a stash on your bench.

news.headline: Eagles' Saquon Barkley: Back at practice
news.summary: Barkley returned to practice Wednesday after his stinger and MRI, trending toward playing Sunday — which would push Bigsby back to a limited change-of-pace role.

news.headline: Marcus Mariota to start at QB in Commanders' Week 3 game as Jayden Daniels seeks opinions on elbow
news.summary: Diggs is healthy and active, but Washington's downgrade to backup QB Marcus Mariota (Daniels re-dislocated his elbow) likely caps his upside Sunday against a tough Seattle defense.

news.headline: Sean McVay hopeful, but unsure of Puka Nacua's availability for Week 3
news.summary: Nacua missed practice again Wednesday with a hip/groin issue and has no firm timeline, putting your opponent's top receiver on track for a game-time call rather than a lock.

news.headline: Jaguars game status report: Brian Thomas Jr. cleared to play Sunday
news.summary: Thomas is off the injury report and fully cleared, removing any doubt about your opponent's second Jaguars starter this week.

news.headline: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart will miss the rest of the regular season with injury
news.summary: With Dart out for the season and Jameis Winston taking over at QB, expect the Giants to lean more on Skattebo and the run game against Tennessee.

SLEEPER — FAAB: $88 of $100 remaining (confirmed live via the league API, waiver_budget_used=12; last night's $93 figure was off by $5, corrected here). Waiver day is Tuesday per your league settings, so today's board carries into next Tuesday's processing.
1. Jonah Coleman (RB, DEN) — the league-wide #1 add this week. Both J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey are dealing with hamstring issues, and Coleman played real starter snaps in Week 2 (10 carries, 3 catches, TD). This is a competitive claim — bid near the top of your range or lose it. Drop Devaughn Vele. FAAB $18.
2. Pat Freiermuth (TE, PIT) — directly fixes your zero-depth TE problem: 9 catches, 78 yards, TD through 2 weeks with real target volume. Pittsburgh's bye isn't Week 7 like Strange's, so he doubles as a real fix for the LAC/JAX bye cluster. Drop Woody Marks (buried in Houston's committee). FAAB $9.
3. Malik Washington (WR, MIA) — Miami's unquestioned WR1 by target share now that Caleb Douglas is out with an ankle injury; a clean upgrade over Michael Wilson's committee role in Arizona. Drop Michael Wilson. FAAB $10.
Total if you take all three: $37, leaving ~$51 banked for the Week 7 bye scramble and any trade-deadline-week (Week 12) pushes.
Hold, don't drop: Tank Bigsby — Saquon Barkley's stinger/MRI has him questionable, and Bigsby would see real work if Barkley sits, in both your leagues. Zay Flowers — still DNP Wednesday on his hamstring, but worth the stash through recovery. Tyler Shough — correctly banked as your Week 7 QB fill-in since New Orleans' bye is Week 8, not 7. Jaguars DEF — still a startable matchup this week (NE implied ~20.8); revisit streaming once the Week 7 bye actually hits rather than churning the spot now.
No K stream needed — Aubrey's spot is fine.

Two names worth checking availability on yourself: Pat Freiermuth (TE, PIT) is the same fix for your Likely/Dart situation as above — with Dart now trending toward possible season-ending surgery, grab real TE insurance today if he's sitting in your pool. Jonah Coleman (RB, DEN) is also widely available and a solid depth add regardless of position need. Michael Mayer (TE, LV) is a short-term streamer only if Brock Bowers is still out closer to kickoff — don't hold him beyond that. trades.text:
SLEEPER — Send Josh Downs (WR, IND) to AdufortheWin84 (roster_id 12) for Dalton Kincaid (TE, BUF). Their roster is stacked at TE (Kincaid, Oronde Gadsden, Michael Mayer, Juwan Johnson — four tight ends for one starting slot) and QB (Prescott/Allen/Hurts), while thin at WR (Golden, London, and an Out Michael Pittman are their only real options) — Downs directly fills that hole for them. For you, Kincaid instantly upgrades your TE room from replacement-level to a weekly starter, permanently solving your thinnest position and the Week 7 bye problem (Strange is out that week too). Checked Weeks 15-17 first: this only touches a bench piece — it doesn't weaken Herbert/Hampton/Brown/Higgins/Diggs/Aubrey/Jaguars DEF for the playoff stretch, it upgrades a real weak spot. One trade-off to know before you send it: if accepted, Michael Wilson reclaims the WR2 job by default — his Week 2 line (2/18) was drawn-penalty and overthrow variance more than lost role, so that's an acceptable downgrade for a full-time starting TE. Not yet sent as of this run.

season.lesson: Started Josh Downs (5.7) over Stefon Diggs sitting on the bench (15.5) in the flex — 9.8 points left on the table. Separately, Zay Flowers' 26-point day ended in a hamstring re-injury that's now clouding Week 2; watch practice reports closely on players who leave games early even when the box score looks great.

Tyler Shough (22.38, waiver QB stash) outscored started QB Justin Herbert (9.88) by 12.5 — not a real swap given Shough's a Saints starter you don't play, but the bigger miss was starting Michael Wilson (3.8) over bench WR Josh Downs (14.2), a 10.4-point gap; the Week 3 lineup already has that fixed. Also: Zay Flowers stayed rostered through a scoreless Week 2 (ruled Out, no IR move) — a wasted bench spot two weeks running.
